audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave K'Sante levels 2, 3, First item and 2+ items while the matching 'why' strings say the opposite ('his sustained chip edges this level', 'starts to out-sustain', 'he out-scales hard'). The packet chart and the 47.85% win rate over 930 games both side with Vladimir there.
audit.why: Vladimir's level-2 Tides of Blood plus Transfusion chip wins before K'Sante has a combo; his AP items and Sanguine Pool out-scale a tank whose armour does nothing against magic. K'Sante's real ownership is level 6 only, before Vladimir has items.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Vladimir / Skill / Skill / K'Sante / Vladimir / Vladimir, matching the packet and the existing whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named Sanguine Pool as the swing but never gave its duration or cooldown.
audit.why: Pool is 2 seconds of untargetability on 28/25/22/19/16s. At rank 1 that is a 28-second window you can play around; maxed it is 16 and effectively always up.
audit.corrected: Spikes and whys now carry the 2s untargetable, 28s at rank 1, 16s maxed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly calls K'Sante's 2-stack Ntofo Strikes a 'Q3 knock-up'; it is a shockwave that pulls in. Grievous Wounds was mentioned only in the item line, never tied to a trade.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' And both Transfusion and Hemoplague heal Vladimir, which is the flagged missing interaction — anti-heal timing, not raw damage, decides an extended trade.
audit.corrected: Pull replaces knock-up; Grievous Wounds is now stated at the level-6 all-in where it changes the result.

edits.before: He charges E poke and heals it with Q while you still lack a combo — his sustained chip edges this level before your W or E.
edits.after: He charges Tides of Blood and heals it straight back with Transfusion while you lack a combo — his chip edges this level.

edits.before: Your Q-W combo comes online and you can W him into terrain for the stun, but his pool can blank it, so it is a coin-flip on his cooldown.
edits.after: Your Q-W lands a terrain stun, but Sanguine Pool's 2s of untargetability blanks it — a coin-flip on whether his 28s pool is up.

edits.before: You out-trade a pre-Rylai Vlad with your bulk, but he pools to dodge your Q3 and W — neither of you reliably wins, so it is skill.
edits.after: You out-trade a pre-Rylai Vlad with your bulk, but he pools out of the Ntofo pull and W — neither reliably wins, so it is skill.

edits.before: Your first tank item is durable, but his first AP item plus pool kiting starts to out-sustain and out-poke your stacking armor.
edits.after: Your first tank item is durable, but his AP item plus Transfusion healing out-sustains armour that does nothing to his magic.

edits.before: Vlad pokes with E charge and Q-heals it back through your only Q — you have no engage threat yet and just farm.
edits.after: Tides of Blood pokes and Transfusion heals it straight back through your only Q — you have no engage threat, so farm.

edits.before: Your Q-W combo is online: bait the pool, then W the charged-up Vlad into terrain for the long stun and Q3 knock-up.
edits.after: Your Q-W is online: bait the pool — 28s at rank 1 — then W him into terrain for the stun and the 2-stack Ntofo pull.

edits.before: All Out is your one clean kill window — R-dash him before he pools, and his low base resists mean your duelist profile can burst him out.
edits.after: All Out is your one clean kill window — R him before Sanguine Pool is up, and carry Grievous Wounds so Transfusion cannot undo it.

edits.before: Rylai/Liandry Vlad with Sanguine Pool dodges your R and Q3 and out-sustains everything — this is his window, not yours.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 2s untargetable on 16s maxed — it blanks your R and your pull, and he out-heals the rest. His window, not yours.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even — you out-position a pre-Rylai Vlad and bank small leads with your bulk, but every time you all-in he can Sanguine Pool to dodge your Q3 knock-up and W stun, so you must force him to burn the pool first. Level 6 is your one clean window: All Out strips your tank stats but gives you a duelist 1v1, and Vlad's low base resists mean your R-dash burst can drop him IF you catch him before pool. Re-cast R to drag him out of his pool's range and finish — this is the last point the matchup is yours.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even — you out-position a pre-Rylai Vlad and bank small leads with your bulk, but any all-in can be blanked by Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability, so force him to burn it first; it is 28s at rank 1 and only 16s maxed. Level 6 is your one clean window: All Out strips your tank stats but gives you a duelist 1v1, and Vlad's low base resists fold to your R burst IF you catch him before pool. Buy Grievous Wounds early, or Transfusion simply undoes the trade — this is the last point the matchup is yours.

edits.before: Bait your Q3 and W, then Sanguine Pool to go untargetable and waste your whole cooldown-reliant combo
edits.after: Bait the Ntofo pull and W, then Sanguine Pool for 2s untargetable to waste your cooldown-reliant combo

notes: Level chart contradicted its own why strings on five of seven rows — the whys were right, the sides were wrong. Also removed the 'Q3 knock-up' phrasing: K'Sante's 2-stack Ntofo Strikes pulls in.
